topic: Exact finite-sample locally private SATE design game. For N>=4 labeled units with arbitrary binary potential-outcome schedules, complete randomization of exactly m treated units, and a common noninteractive epsilon-local-DP channel protecting (W,Yobs), jointly minimize worst-schedule expected cardinality among randomized exact 1-alpha confidence sets for the finite-population SATE. Prove schedule-orbit reduction and sufficiency of the fourteen nonconstant four-input staircase patterns; formulate fixed-channel confidence inference as an exact primal-dual LP and common-channel optimization as an attained degree-N polynomial game; develop algebraic or positive-tolerance global certificates; and characterize the parameter cells and actual boundaries where a balanced design with randomized response after a nontrivial binary partition is globally optimal. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact derivations give the orbit generating-function kernel, fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, fixed-channel LP, and polynomial-dual global lower bounds. Independent exact reruns certify a nonbinary exclusion interval [999.9,1000.1], disprove the convex-utility shortcut, and bracket the unrestricted N=4, alpha=2/5, lambda=1000 value in [2.58227914,2.58228508], with every optimizer balanced for lambda>=1000; no exact literature collision was found, while consumer translation requires a hidden-assignment protocol. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Make the simultaneous lower certificate attain equality at a specified optimizing channel and continue it across a nontrivial parameter cell to identify an actual boundary of the balanced-binary equality set. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the full fourteen-weight N=4 global bracket within 1e-5 and 100000 channel cells; this passed in one cell using 2,825,761 exact vertex-tensor bounds, so the next kill test is failure of optimizer-attaining certificate extraction. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_private_sate_design_game.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the exact locally private SATE confidence problem be reduced to schedule orbits and fourteen nonconstant four-input staircase outputs, with fixed-channel inference characterized by a finite primal-dual LP?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact-randomization work fixes the observation experiment, while causal-LDP work studies asymptotic estimation and staircase results optimize convex single-draw information utilities. Here schedule-wise exact coverage, randomized set inclusion, and expected cardinality are coupled after an N-fold channel composition. The prior CausalSmith orbit construction supplies finite aggregation and polynomial attainment machinery, but its squared-error posterior decision step must be replaced by a coverage LP valid on zero-probability transcript faces; moreover, ordinary extreme-point arguments do not by themselves prove the required Blackwell refinement to the fourteen nonconstant staircase patterns.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An orbit-kernel theorem, a constructive Blackwell refinement of every feasible four-input epsilon-LDP channel to the fourteen nonconstant staircase outputs, and explicit finite primal and dual LPs with equality, attainment, and complementary slackness for every fixed channel.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly connects randomized experiments, source-level protection of treatment and outcomes, and the inferential cost of privacy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomized experiments identify causal effects -> treatment and outcomes may require local protection -> privacy noise changes valid inference -> exact finite-population confidence design must optimize the privatized experiment itself

method_exemplars.technique: Represent finite-alphabet LDP channels through staircase columns and prove finite-output reduction using privacy-polytope geometry and channel refinement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The protected pair (W,Yobs) has four values, precisely the finite alphabet whose nonconstant staircase rays must support the proposed channel reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use test-confidence duality and least-favorable mixing to optimize worst-case expected confidence-region size under coverage constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Expected SATE-set cardinality is the discrete counterpart of expected confidence-region measure, and the exact constraints form a finite minimax decision problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate binary potential-outcome schedules under complete randomization and invert finite-sample randomization tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nonprivate exact finite-population inference layer that must be reconstructed for privatized transcript probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: For N=4, can an optimizer-attaining global polynomial certificate be continued over a nonempty parameter cell to identify an actual boundary of the region where balanced assignment and randomized response after a binary partition are globally optimal?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known binary-mechanism optimality theorems optimize single-draw f-divergences or asymptotic losses. In the SATE game, an inner exact-confidence LP makes channel value a nonconvex lower envelope of degree-N polynomial pieces, so likelihood-ratio sorting and convex-utility reductions do not establish global optimality. The prior orbit saddle argument gives pointwise support complementarity but explicitly stops before a closed-form classification. Numerical subdivision can bracket the value without producing a dual that is tight at the candidate channel, while residual polynomials may vanish on privacy-polytope faces and the optimizer or boundary may be algebraic rather than rational.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicitly specified algebraic optimizing channel and attaining confidence-LP dual, a finite SOS, Bernstein, Handelman, or facewise identity proving their value globally on an open parameter cell, and a sign-certified polynomial equality defining one genuine boundary of balanced-binary optimality.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing treats privacy mechanism, treatment allocation, and confidence precision as one experiment-design problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Private experimentation limits accessible information -> privacy degrades confidence precision -> mechanism and allocation jointly determine utility -> exact phase boundaries should reveal when balanced binary designs are truly optimal

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce LDP optimization to staircase-pattern weights and compare binary and randomized-response candidates across privacy regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired phase diagram lies on the same staircase simplex, with an exact causal decision-game objective replacing an f-divergence.

method_exemplars.technique: Adjoin Fritz John critical equations to moment-SOS relaxations and use finite convergence to recover exact minimizers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each fixed-dual piece is a polynomial optimized over a simplex or face-defined semialgebraic set, matching the certificate target.

method_exemplars.technique: Expose tight confidence-procedure duals through least-favorable alternatives and inverted randomized tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A least-favorable distribution can identify the LP dual whose polynomial residual must be certified nonnegative throughout the cell.

open_problems.open_problem: When does hiding assignment inside a common local channel have the same exact minimax SATE confidence risk as revealing assignment or allowing treatment-aware outcome channels, and when is the loss strictly positive?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Randomization inference ordinarily treats W as analyst-known, whereas a joint channel on (W,Yobs) can conceal W. Revealing W, allowing the encoder to condition on W, and using assignment randomness as public randomness generate different finite statistical experiments. Existing causal-LDP comparisons use estimation MSE rather than exact schedule-wise coverage and worst-cardinality risk, so an algebraically optimal hidden-assignment channel may neither dominate nor be operationally equivalent to a standard trial protocol.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-experiment comparison theorem giving explicit garbling maps in regimes of equal risk and, in every strict regime, a labeled potential-outcome schedule family plus an exact primal-dual witness for a positive minimax expected-cardinality gap.

writing_exemplar.why: Its explicit separation of joint and customized privatization scenarios provides the natural vocabulary for the protocol distinction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment and outcomes may both be sensitive -> local protection admits operationally different information structures -> those structures have different estimation behavior -> exact confidence risk requires a protocol-level equivalence or separation theorem

method_exemplars.technique: Compare finite experiments by constructing stochastic garbling maps, and prove strict separation through a decision problem with unequal risks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested equality-or-gap statement is a comparison of transcript experiments indexed by fixed potential-outcome schedules.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate public-coin and private-coin local protocols using explicit mechanisms and matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Treatment assignment can act as public randomness, making protocol timing and visibility structurally analogous.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert the known complete-randomization law to construct exact finite-population SATE confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the revealed-assignment experiment forming one endpoint of the desired comparison.

open_problems.open_problem: Under approximate (epsilon,delta)-local privacy on (W,Yobs), does any finite universal output reduction preserve the exact SATE confidence game, or can a larger-output extreme channel strictly improve minimax expected cardinality?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pure-LDP output reduction relies on likelihood-ratio constraints whose extremal columns are two-level staircase patterns. Delta slack changes the privacy polytope qualitatively; for the four inputs representing (W,Yobs), current results do not supply a complete extreme-point classification or universal output bound and already exhibit new configurations beyond smaller alphabets. Consequently, the fourteen-pattern refinement cannot simply be reused, and the exact causal decision objective could select an approximate-private extreme channel absent from pure-LDP geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a finite-output refinement theorem and attained polynomial-game formulation for four-input (epsilon,delta)-LDP exact SATE inference, or an explicit parameter tuple, schedule family, and larger-output extreme channel with a dual certificate proving every fourteen-pattern mechanism strictly suboptimal.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames approximate local privacy as a qualitative change in finite-channel geometry and places four inputs just beyond the completely characterized cases.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pure-LDP extreme mechanisms are structured -> delta slack changes the channel polytope -> four-input channels have unclassified extreme configurations -> exact SATE design tests whether those configurations possess causal-inference value

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize channel extremality through feasible perturbations and linear-system rank conditions, including star configurations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination requires either an exhaustive description or a separating example for approximate-private extreme channels on exactly four inputs.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine arbitrary pure-LDP channels into staircase columns while preserving the relevant decision utility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its channel-refinement step is precisely what must be repaired or disproved once delta slack is introduced.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct exact finite-sample SATE confidence intervals by efficient inversion over binary potential-outcome tables.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact confidence target against which approximate-private channels and randomized rules must be evaluated.

literature_map:
Ohnishi and Awan (2025, JMLR, arXiv:2301.01616) are the closest causal-LDP anchor: randomized experiments, joint/customized privatization, plug-in intervals, and minimax MSE, but no exact finite-population confidence game.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Statistics in Medicine, doi:10.1002/sim.6384) give exact binary-outcome SATE confidence sets under complete randomization without privacy.
Li and Ding (2016, Statistics in Medicine, doi:10.1002/sim.6924) accelerate exact SATE confidence construction using hypergeometric intervals and stochastic ordering.
Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2305.09906) reduce balanced-design exact computation to O(N log N) permutation tests.
Schafer and Stark (2009, JASA, doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.tm07420) supply the minimax expected-size confidence-set decision framework.
Karwa and Vadhan (2018, ITCS, arXiv:1711.03908) prove finite-sample private confidence-interval and expected-size results for a central-DP normal mean, not local-DP SATE.
Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016, JMLR, arXiv:1407.1338) prove staircase extremality and finite LP reduction for convex information utilities, with binary/RR optimality only in selected regimes.
Holohan, Leith, and Mason (2017, Linear Algebra and its Applications, arXiv:1605.05510) characterize selected pure-LDP polytope vertices.
Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa (2026, arXiv:2606.07443) prove sort-partition-randomize optimality for binary testing, a close single-draw f-divergence analogue.
Acharya, Canonne, Freitag, and Tyagi (2019, AISTATS, arXiv:1808.02174) show that bespoke one-bit and public-coin mechanisms can change locally private testing performance.
Chen et al. (2024, AISTATS, arXiv:2311.04375) jointly study private experiment design and confidence width, but not exact finite-population minimax cardinality.
Mai (2023, arXiv:2205.04254), Aqel and Ali (2022, doi:10.1016/j.cam.2022.114430), and Bienstock et al. (2023, arXiv:2011.08347) provide candidate polynomial-certificate machinery without an LDP causal-game application.
Rawat et al. (2026, arXiv:2606.09161) and Elangovan and Jog (2024, doi:10.1109/ISIT57864.2024.10619506) show approximate-LDP geometry changes qualitatively at the four-input boundary.
Searches combining exact randomization inference, local privacy, minimax expected cardinality, and joint mechanism/design optimization found no paper directly occupying the stated intersection.
